name: v7 fixed-space SBDF2 step-count qualification
layout_evidence: Native Galerkin plans use len(model.r) lines, with 66 split quadrature nodes apportioned 44+11+11. Native FD plans use the interior width from model.rhs_shape, 175 for FD176. The FFT uses these interior lines rather than the 177 FD grid coordinates including two walls. The runner checks reconstructed model sizes.
anchor_reuse: Reuse completed equilibrated-reference joint CPU/CUDA pairs only on identical runtime dependency hashes, configuration, seed, checkpoint and solver metadata. Use graph settings from frozen.template and retain all archived manifest hashes, including audit-only files. For deterministic methods use block 1, irrespective of time. If unavailable, stop unless the caller explicitly requests all anchor pairs be rerun and the reason is recorded.
qualification: For every seed require all original grid/time/full/near velocity/curl metrics and sustained wake against both references. For each field/grid/time also require E(candidate,128)*(1+E(128,ref))+E(128,ref) <= 0.005 for each reference, excluding apparent spatial/time cancellation. On the same-space sequence from candidate through r128, the per-norm maximum gap to the anchor must be nonincreasing with rate up to the stated absolute slack, and all finer arms must have direct passes.
confirmation: Choose by minimum step count, never runtime. Confirm all chosen seeds with the identical CPU configuration and synchronized physical checkpoints. Require both direct CPU accuracy and matching CPU/GPU fields/probes. If confirmation fails, retain the failure and check the next eligible rate.
interpretation: A finite empirical accuracy/trend check, not a continuum error bound or an observed-order proof. SBDF2 and per-step nonlinear method are unchanged. Each marching evaluation issues one inverse and one forward batched FFT. Galerkin batches contain 3 inverse and 2 forward field transforms, FD batches contain 4 inverse and 1 forward. Counts exclude setup and priming. Screen runtimes are not formal isolated ranking evidence.
